hero_desc: I build Go and Java services for a pharma distribution platform. Most of my work is on the latency path: running calls concurrently, batching queries, and cancelling cleanly.
intro_tagline: The performance side is what I enjoy most — goroutine fan-out, context cancellation, and knowing when a problem genuinely needs concurrency versus a better data model.
subTitle: Backend engineer, mostly Go and Java.
bio_desc: I'm a final-year Computer Science student at SRM University AP, currently an SDE-1 at SwishX in Bengaluru, where I build backend services for a pharma distribution platform. Much of my work is making requests that touch several services return fast — running independent calls concurrently so a response costs the slowest one instead of the sum of all of them, batching what would otherwise be hundreds of round trips, and making sure that when a request is cancelled, the work still in flight gets torn down with it.

I built a 6-level sales hierarchy engine on recursive PostgreSQL CTEs, automated an MOQ-based cashback flow that replaced a manual points-grant process across 90 schemes and 568 rules, and shipped a CMS backend in Go delivering 20+ REST APIs with Redis caching and S3 storage.

On the side: a RAG-based Git analyzer that answers questions about a repo's commit history, an AI resume builder, and a roommate-finding app. Oracle Certified Professional for Java SE 17, and an open-source contributor. Away from the screen I volunteer with NSS — blood donation camps and beach clean-ups, mostly.
